nodes.description: A recognisable but non-specific facial gestalt comprising broad forehead, deep-set eyes, upslanting palpebral fissures, smooth philtrum and thin upper lip. The gestalt is bound to the generic facial-shape term rather than to any one of its components, and its five constituent features are named as sequelae below so the graph shows what the gestalt is made of.

nodes.description: Three copies of the interval raise expression of the genes it contains. BMPR1A, GRID1 and NRG3 are the named candidates; BMPR1A and GRID1 were proposed for the cardiac phenotype on the basis of their roles in cardiac structure and function. No single interval gene has been shown to account for the duplication phenotype, so the dosage change is modelled at the level of the interval.

nodes.description: The 10q22.3q23.3 region carries two directly oriented low-copy repeats, LCR3 and LCR4. Non-allelic homologous recombination between them produces reciprocal deletion and duplication products, which is why the two syndromes share breakpoints. Rearrangements with unique breakpoints also occur in the region.
